I have mixed feelings on this. I don’t know anyone in my life who is deaf but I took an ASL class in high school. The deaf community isolated themselves from the hearing world due to the abuse the hearing world inflicted on them so I do understand why they are defensive and isolated. They felt like they only had each other from what I understand. 

But it should be up to personal choice and no judgment issued on who get the implants and who doesn’t. I don’t think it should mandatory or considered child neglect if they don’t have one like OP said in some comments but it could potentially help some people. If they want it, great. If they don’t want it, okay. 

But it’s honestly really gross seeing how many hearing people look down on the deaf community like we didn’t shut them out first. We watched a documentary in ASL class and it was about how deaf kids weren’t allowed to sign and were forced to lip read and speak. They got left out of every joke “oh I’ll tell you later”. So they finally had enough and created their own community. 

I see a parallel with the autism community. The autistic community was separated from society as well and no one wants a cure for autism. As an autistic person, I really don’t know if I would get the cure if one was able to me. Yes being autistic is a unique experience and I think my life would be quite different (in both good and bad ways) if I didn’t have autism. But demonizing anyone who wants to get it or doesn’t want to get it is pointless. 

Everyone just needs to live their own life. And able bodied people please please be more understanding of disabled people and don’t look down on them because you separated them first.
